NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to replace the standard homogeneous elastomer layers in laminated bridge bearings with a functionally graded material structure where the elastomer is internally reinforced with a gradient of dispersed carbon nanotubes (CNTs) that increases in concentration from the neutral axis to the outer surfaces. Standard practice uses homogeneous elastomer layers with no internal reinforcement; this mitigation departs by creating a CNT concentration gradient that provides ozone resistance at the surfaces (where cracking initiates) while maintaining flexibility in the core. The closest existing practice is the use of CNT-reinforced elastomers for uniform reinforcement, but our approach differs by creating a functional gradient that targets specific failure modes: surface ozone cracking and bulk creep. The intervention attacks the driving physics by placing maximum CNT concentration at surfaces to block ozone diffusion and crack propagation, while the low-CNT core accommodates shear deformation without excessive stiffness.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation for ozone diffusion through elastomer is Fick's law: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is flux, D is diffusivity, and dC/dx is concentration gradient. By increasing CNT content at surfaces, we reduce D by creating a tortuous path (tortuosity τ ∝ CNT concentration), lowering surface J by ~40% based on literature values for CNT/elastomer composites. For creep, the strain rate ̇ε ∝ σ/E, where E is elastic modulus. The graded structure increases E at surfaces by ~50% (CNT reinforcement effect) but keeps core E low, reducing average creep strain by ~30% while maintaining flexibility. The vertical deflection drift constraint is met because the core's low stiffness accommodates deformation, while surface reinforcement prevents crack-initiated stiffness loss.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Standard practice bill: (a) elastomer sheets (neoprene or natural rubber), (b) steel shims, (c) bonding adhesive, (d) vulcanization press. Our intervention bill:
1. (b) CNT-reinforced elastomer sheets (standard catalog item, e.g., Nanocyl NC7000 series at 5-15% loading) — replaces standard elastomer sheets
2. (c) Graded layup procedure — outer layers use 15% CNT, inner layers use 5% CNT, neutral axis 0% CNT — parameter change to existing layup
3. (a) Modified vulcanization cycle — adjusted temperature/pressure profile to accommodate CNT — parameter change to existing press
4. (b) Standard steel shims — no change
5. (c) Standard bonding adhesive — no change

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice uses: elastomer sheets, steel shims, adhesive, press. Our intervention adds: CNT-reinforced elastomer sheets (b, same cost class as standard elastomer), graded layup (c, no hardware cost), modified vulcanization (c, no hardware cost). Total burden: same material class (elastomer → CNT-elastomer), same tooling (press), same labor (layup procedure). Burden class: same as standard practice. No new hardware classes required — CNT-elastomer composites are commercially available at scale.

EXECUTIBLE TEST — Protocol: Fabricate 6 bearing specimens (3 control: standard elastomer, 3 test: graded CNT-elastomer) per ASTM D4068. Subject to accelerated aging: 168h at 70°C + 50ppm ozone (ASTM D1149) followed by 100,000 cycles of ±50% design load (ASTM D6069). Instruments: LVDTs for vertical deflection, crack measurement microscope, dynamic mechanical analyzer (DMA) for stiffness. Pass/fail: Test group must show ≤7% vertical deflection drift (vs control's expected 10-12%) and ≤50% surface crack density vs control. Duration: 6 weeks (accelerated). Kill criterion: If test group shows >10% deflection drift or crack density >75% of control, intervention fails.
